zh.title: IATA：2026年6月全球航空貨運需求年增8.5%
zh.summary: IATA公布2026年6月全球航空貨運市場資料，以貨噸公里計的需求較2025年同期成長8.5%，國際航線成長9.6%；運能成長4.4%。北美為成長最強地區，中東因與去年同期基期偏低有關。需求成長超越全球貿易與運能，但IATA提醒中東衝突與美國關稅政策仍為風險。
body: 國際航空運輸協會（IATA）發布2026年6月全球航空貨運市場資料。以貨噸公里（CTK）計算的總需求較2025年6月成長8.5%，其中國際航線成長9.6%；以可用貨噸公里（ACTK）計算的運能則較去年同期成長4.4%，國際航線成長4.9%。
IATA理事長Willie Walsh表示，6月航空貨運需求年增8.5%，北美為成長最大貢獻地區，所有地區需求均較去年為正。他指出需求成長在全球及除拉丁美洲與加勒比海以外的所有地區均超越運能，且成長速度高於全球貿易，受高價值科技產品與急件運輸帶動。他同時提醒，中東持續的衝突與美國重新聚焦關稅政策仍為風險因素。
按地區觀察，亞太航空公司6月貨運需求年增7.9%，運能成長4.3%。北美航空公司需求年增13.1%，為各地區最強表現，運能成長6.2%。歐洲航空公司需求年增6.9%，運能成長3.7%。
中東航空公司需求年增5.6%，運能成長2.5%。IATA指出，該月結果雖屬成長，但正向數據受到比較基期偏低的影響，因2025年6月受軍事衝突干擾而特別疲弱。拉丁美洲與加勒比海航空公司需求年增3.5%，為各地區最弱，運能成長9.8%。非洲航空公司需求年增4.7%，運能年減7.1%。
IATA另指出，6月全球貿易年增5.2%。噴射燃料價格較上月下跌20%，但仍較去年同期高出45.8%。全球製造業產出採購經理人指數（PMI）下降0.5點至53.0，新出口訂單指數連續第四個月低於50，報49.4，顯示航空貨運成長由特定貿易流向帶動，而非全球出口廣泛回升。主要貿易航線中，亞洲至北美成長最強，其次為亞洲區內、歐洲至亞洲及非洲至亞洲；與波斯灣相關的航線則持續受中東衝突影響。

en.title: IATA: Global Air Cargo Demand Rose 8.5% Year-on-Year in June 2026
en.summary: IATA released June 2026 global air cargo market data showing total demand measured in cargo tonne-kilometers increased 8.5% versus June 2025, with international operations up 9.6%. Capacity rose 4.4%. North America was the strongest growth contributor. Middle East results were skewed positive by a weak year-earlier comparison. Demand growth outpaced capacity and global trade, but IATA cited Middle East hostilities and US tariff focus as risks.
body: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) released data for June 2026 global air cargo markets. Total demand, measured in cargo tonne-kilometers (CTK), increased by 8.5% compared to June 2025, with international operations rising 9.6%. Capacity, measured in available cargo tonne-kilometers (ACTK), increased by 4.4% year-on-year, or 4.9% for international operations.

IATA Director General Willie Walsh said air cargo demand grew 8.5% year-on-year in June, with North America the strongest contributor and all regions in positive territory. He noted that demand growth outpaced capacity at the global level and in all regions except Latin America and the Caribbean, and that demand also grew faster than global trade, supported by high-value technology products and urgent shipments. He cautioned that risks remain, including continuing hostilities in the Middle East and a renewed focus on tariffs by the US.

By region, Asia-Pacific airlines saw 7.9% year-on-year growth in air cargo demand in June, with capacity up 4.3%. North American carriers recorded a 13.1% increase, the strongest performance of all regions, with capacity up 6.2%. European carriers saw demand rise 6.9%, with capacity up 3.7%.

Middle Eastern carriers saw a 5.6% year-on-year increase in demand, with capacity up 2.5%. IATA noted the results were skewed positive because the comparison is to June 2025, which was particularly weak for Middle East carriers due to disruptions from military conflict. Latin American and Caribbean carriers saw the weakest performance at 3.5% growth, with capacity up 9.8%. African airlines recorded 4.7% demand growth, with capacity decreasing by 7.1% year-on-year.

IATA also reported that global trade increased by 5.2% year-on-year. Jet fuel prices fell by 20% month-on-month in June but remained 45.8% above year-earlier levels. The Global Manufacturing Output PMI fell 0.5 points to 53.0, while the New Export Orders Index remained below 50 for a fourth consecutive month at 49.4, suggesting air cargo growth was driven by specific trade flows rather than a broad-based increase in global exports. Asia-North America recorded the strongest growth among major trade lanes, followed by Within Asia, Europe-Asia, and Africa-Asia, while Gulf-linked corridors remained disrupted by the conflict in the Middle East.
